images.caption: Parliament House, Hobart has been the meeting place of the Government of Tasmania since 1841. The building was originally designed as a customs house, and from 1841 until 1904 when the customs offices were relocated, the building served both purposes. It is located on Salamanca Place in Hobart, Tasmania, Australia. It is the home of the Parliament of Tasmania, which is a bicameral parliament consisting of the Tasmanian Legislative Council (Upper House) and the Tasmanian House of Assembly (Lower House) [Wikipedia.org]
images.alt: Parliament House, Hobart has been the meeting place of the Government of Tasmania since 1841. The building was originally designed as a customs house, and from 1841 until 1904 when the customs offices were relocated, the building served both purposes. It is located on Salamanca Place in Hobart, Tasmania, Australia. It is the home of the Parliament of Tasmania, which is a bicameral parliament consisting of the Tasmanian Legislative Council (Upper House) and the Tasmanian House of Assembly (Lower House) [Wikipedia.org]

images.filename: Cadburys Chocolate Factory Claremont Tasmania Harry Kelly 1950.jpg
images.caption: Image is of a promotional poster commissioned by Cadbury-Fry-Pascall Ltd showcasing Cadbury's Chocolate Factory at Claremont, Tasmania, Australia. The aerial illustration by Harry Kelly features a snow-capped kunanyi/Mount Wellington, Windermere Bay and the River Derwent. The poster includes the caption, "By mountain and sea", which appeared on many of the factory's early advertising materials. The original image is located within the Tasmanian Archives and The State Library, in the collection of W.E.L.H. Crowther.
images.alt: Image is of a promotional poster commissioned by Cadbury-Fry-Pascall Ltd showcasing Cadbury's Chocolate Factory at Claremont, Tasmania, Australia. The aerial illustration by Harry Kelly features a snow-capped kunanyi/Mount Wellington, Windermere Bay and the River Derwent. The original image is located within the Tasmanian Archives and The State Library, in the collection of W.E.L.H. Crowther.

images.caption: Theatre Royal is an historic performing arts venue in central Hobart, Tasmania. It is the oldest continually operating theatre in Australia; Noël Coward once called it "a dream of a theatre" and Laurence Olivier launched a national appeal for its reconstruction in the 1940s.
